concept: Kbd prints the name of a key the way a case prints its legends, then gives the word a little height so it reads as the key itself: a flat cap with a hard lower edge. It is a name, not a part, so nothing in it presses, hovers or takes focus.

default_to_avoid.pattern: keycap chip: a rounded pill with a thin outline and a grey fill, the same look as a tag or a badge
default_to_avoid.why_not: With no height it reads as a status chip and not as a key, and a soft blur shadow makes it look pressable when it is only a name.

default_to_avoid.pattern: keycap drawn as a raised button with the part shadow and a hover lift
default_to_avoid.why_not: A key name is not a mechanism; the shadow of a control tells a hand to press it, and the keycap in running text must not pull the eye from the line.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): the band names are printed on the case beside the keys that choose them
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): small flat keys whose height shows as a dark lower edge, not as a blurred shadow
system/FORM.md control class: a key is raised and lit on the top-left edge, and printing is flat ink

derivation.consequence: shadows are short and soft; a unit never floats more than its material height
derivation.form: The cap casts no blur. Its height is a lit hairline on the top-left edge and a hard lower edge in line.ring, so it is raised by about two pixels and no more.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only
derivation.form: The key name is set in the same grotesk as the text around it, in medium weight at the label size, so it sits in a line without a second face.

derivation.consequence: hover only darkens a key's ink a step, because a real key does not rise when you approach it
derivation.form: A Kbd names a key and is not one, so it has no hover, active or focus state at all and keeps the default cursor.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The cap is the knob plastic with primary ink and a ring-coloured edge, never orange, so a shortcuts list does not compete with the unit's one key.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes
derivation.form: Primary ink on surface.knob measures 11.0 to 1 in light and 7.2 to 1 in dark, and the edge is line.ring, which holds 3.2 to 1 or more on the body and the page.

options.name: soft raised cap with the part shadow
flat cap with a hard lower edge
cap nested in a recessed socket

variants.reason: B shows height with an edge the size of a key side and stays inside the line box; A is a blurred chip that looks pressable and C is 30px tall with a double frame that breaks the line in running text.

root.why: A kbd element holding the key name in the label size and medium weight, centred in a cap that is at least 24px square so one letter and a word both look like keys.

combo.why: A kbd that groups several caps and the signs between them, so a chord such as Ctrl plus K is one unit in the line and does not break between its keys.

join.why: The printed plus between two caps, in secondary ink and hidden from assistive tech, which reads the word plus from the hidden text instead.

hidden.why: Words only a screen reader gets: the spoken name of a symbol key such as an arrow and the word plus between the keys of a chord.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the cap keeps a real border in the text colour on all four sides, so the lower edge and the key shape survive.
